==English== ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:chaungen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|changen}}, {{m|enm|chaungen}}, from {{der|en|fro|changier}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|cambiāre}}, from {{der|en|la|cambio|cambīre|to exchange, barter}}, derived from the noun {{m|la|cambium||change}} (whence was loaned the English {{lg|doublet}} {{dbt|en|cambium|notext=1}}), from {{der|en|cel-gau|cambion}}, earlier {{m|cel-gau||*kambyom|change}}, related to {{der|en|cel-pro|*kambos||twisted, crooked}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro||*(s)ḱh₂(e)mbos}}, {{m|ine-pro||*(s)kh₂(e)mbos|crooked}}. More at {{l|en|skimp}}, {{l|en|scam}}; see also {{m+|ine-pro|*kh₂em-}}. Cognate with {{cog|it|cambiare}}, {{cog|pt|cambiar}}, {{cog|ro|schimba}}, {{cog|scn|canciari}}, {{cog|es|cambiar}}. Used in English since the 13th century. {{displaced|enm|wenden}}, from {{m|ang|wendan||to turn, change}} (whence {{m|en|wend}}). The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|change}}, {{m|enm|chaunge}}, from {{der|en|fro|change}}, from the verb {{m|fro|changier}}. See also {{m|en|exchange}}. Possibly related from the same source is Old English {{m|ang|gombe}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈt͡ʃeɪnd͡ʒ/|[ˈt͡ʃʰeɪ̯nd͡ʒ]|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-change.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈt͡ʃɛjnd͡ʒ/|a=SSB}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-change.ogg|a=SSB}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈt͡ʃæɪnd͡ʒ/|[ˈt͡ʃʰæ̝ɪ̯nd͡ʒ]|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/t͡ʃend͡ʒ/|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/t͡ʃeːnd͡ʒ/|a=Northern England,Ireland [[w:Monophthongization|monophthongization]]}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪndʒ|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|change}} ===Verb=== {{wikidata lexeme|L33}} {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To become something different. #: {{ux|en|The tadpole '''changed''' into a frog.}} #: {{ux|en|Stock prices are constantly '''changing'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|ergative}} To make something into something else. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|I|I|1|Lo I the man, whoſe Muſe whilome did maske,
As time her taught in lowly Shepheards weeds,

For trumpets ſterne to '''chaunge''' mine oaten reeds,
And ſinge of Knights and Ladies gentle deeds{{…}}|stanza=1}} #* {{RQ:Economist|title=The climate of Tibet: Pole-land|date=2013-05-11|volume=407|issue=8835|url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2013/05/11/pole-land|page=80|passage=Of all the transitions brought about on the Earth’s surface by temperature change, the melting of ice into water is the starkest.
